doc.title: Nat Hentoff interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

title: His mother, Frances Sweeney and Ben Webster ballads
summary: His mother could not understand his jazz; after Frances Sweeney died he played Ben Webster ballads repeatedly.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well let me go back to your — I love this book, Boston Boy.
You talk about your mother really questioning almost your sanity about your choice of what you were pursuing.

She couldn’t understand it. She said it all sounds the same, this jazz. And I remember when Frances Sweeney, who is prominent in the book, died, the only way I could get some kind of consolation was to play Ben Webster ballads again and again and again. And I almost drove my mother crazy.
Do you think she’d be proud of what your accomplishments have been?
Oh I guess so, so would my father, just because the name is around.
Yeah, as you said, there’s a lot of longevity here, you’ve been around for so long.
